flow: Pick queue serve failing - warehouse idle
what_breaks: GET /picker/order is failing, so pickers cannot pull work. The warehouse floor stops and every order behind it misses its RFD. Same shape as the Polaris next-task failure but with a physical queue behind it.
runbook: Check the last deploy. Confirm SO creation is healthy first - the picking query is gated on zohoOrderCreationStatus == SALES_ORDER_CREATED, so an SO outage starves this queue without erroring.
notes: Distinguish 'query erroring' from 'queue legitimately empty' - only the former lands here. For the latter see pick-queue-starved. Per-warehouse mutex means one warehouse can stall alone; capture warehouseId in triage.

flow: Pick queue serve failing - warehouse idle
what_breaks: Some pickers are failing to pull their next order
runbook: Check whether it is one warehouse or one picker - a stuck assignment (COMPLETE_ALREADY_ASSIGNED_ORDER_FIRST) is a legitimate rejection, not an outage.
notes: Legitimate floor from pickers who already hold an order. Exclude that error message before setting the number.

what_breaks: Pickers cannot close orders. The order stays at PICKER_ASSIGNED holding the picker, and batch selections may be half-written - order_item_batches is the record QC and invoicing both read.
runbook: Check whether batches were written for the affected orders before letting pickers retry - a partial batch write is worse than a clean failure.
notes: Batch writes feed QC, invoice and the Zoho decrement, so a failure here propagates three stages downstream. PICKED_QTY_IS_NOT_EQUAL_TO_ORDERED_QTY is a legitimate rejection - exclude it or it dominates the count.

what_breaks: Some pick completions are failing
runbook: Sample orderIds. Repeated failures on one order usually mean a batch/stock mismatch, not a code fault.
notes: Expect a real floor from quantity-mismatch rejections. Baseline before trusting the number.

what_breaks: Invoices are not being generated. Forward shipment is gated on invoice (status 55) and booked at QC_COMPLETED (61), so nothing ships. Orders pile up fully picked and un-dispatchable.
runbook: Check Zoho health first - if the SO alerts are also firing, fix Zoho and these recover. Otherwise sample error_message for a tax/eway/GST validation cause.
notes: This is the chokepoint of the whole fulfilment chain: SO -> pick -> QC -> INVOICE(55) -> shipment(61) -> manifest -> dispatch. Everything downstream stalls behind it. INVOICE_BLOCKED_SALES_ORDER_PENDING_EDIT and INVOICE_BLOCKED_SALES_ORDER_NOT_READY are expected gates, not failures - keep them out of this metric.

what_breaks: Some invoices are failing to generate
runbook: Usually one order's data - missing eway number above the 50k threshold is the classic.
notes: E-way is required at >= 50,000 (ERROR_KEY.EWAY_NUMBER_IS_REQUIRED...). That is a data problem for ops, not an engineering incident.

what_breaks: Invoice generation starts and never completes - a downstream step hangs. The order sits at QC with no invoice and no error, so no error-rate alert can see it.
signal: CREATE_INVOICE_STEP_TIMING phase=start vs the summary log
runbook: Read the per-step logs for a hung orderId to see which step never returned. Zoho PDF fetch is the usual suspect.
notes: THE CODE WAS BUILT FOR THIS: the phase='start' marker is emitted before any work specifically so a hang that never reaches the summary still leaves a record (orders.service.ts:20046-20054). Started-minus-completed is a designed-in hang detector - use it. Confirm the exact summary phase value before writing the filter.

what_breaks: Invoice generation is slower than normal
runbook: Per-step logs identify the dominant step directly - that is what they were added for.
notes: One of the few places in the codebase with real step-level latency. Use it rather than inferring from REST_SLOW_CALL.

what_breaks: An invoice follow-up task (mark-sent / finalize-PDF / sealed-Rx-PDF) was dropped after its last attempt. The invoice exists but its downstream artefact does not, and SQS will not retry.
runbook: Take orderId/invoiceId from the log and re-drive via the reconciliation endpoint - that is the designed retry path once the queue has given up.
notes: MAX_RECEIVE_COUNT IS ONLY 2 (invoice-async-task.constants.ts:51), so a message is dropped after two attempts - much less forgiving than it sounds. Pair with INVOICE_ASYNC_TASK_LAST_ATTEMPT_WARNING as an earlier warning of the same thing.

what_breaks: Invoice follow-up tasks are reaching their final attempt
runbook: This fires BEFORE the drop - treat it as the actionable one and inv-task-dropped as the confirmation.
notes: Deliberately paired: last-attempt warns, dropped confirms. If the warning is quiet but drops appear, the warning is not firing where you think it is.

what_breaks: Orders cannot be marked dispatched. Handover to the courier is not recorded, so tracking never starts and the customer sees no movement on a parcel that has physically left.
runbook: Check whether the shipment exists for the affected orders (status_id >= 61). Dispatch marking on an order with no shipment is a different bug from dispatch marking failing outright.
notes: Time-sensitive in a way the other alerts are not: it fires during the courier pickup window, and a missed window costs a full day of transit. Bias toward paging even at low volume during pickup hours.

what_breaks: Some dispatch markings are failing
runbook: Check MARK_DISPATCHED_PROMISES in the same window - it records the batch outcome and shows how many of a bulk mark succeeded.
notes: MARK_DISPATCHED_PROMISES gives per-batch success/failure counts, so it is the better triage signal once this fires.

what_breaks: GET /ops/manifestedOrders is failing, so warehouse staff cannot see what to hand over. The floor is blocked even though every order behind it is ready.
runbook: Read path - check the last deploy first. Ops will report this as 'the manifest page is blank'.
notes: Read-path breakage that stops physical work. Cheap to detect, and the kind of regression a UI change ships without noticing.

what_breaks: Manifest list failing intermittently
runbook: Often a filter/date-range shape rather than a global break.
notes: Capture the query params in triage.

flow: Gatepass creation failing - goods stuck at the gate
what_breaks: Vendor deliveries cannot be booked in. Nothing can be inwarded because a gatepass number is a hard prerequisite for starting a GRN, so trucks queue at the gate and stock never enters the building.
runbook: Check error_message for DUPLICATE_ACTIVE_GATEPASS (an open gatepass already exists for that warehouse+vendor+bill) or INVALID_CARRIER_PARTNER - both are data rejections, not outages.
notes: Head of the whole inward chain: gatepass -> GRN -> Zoho bill -> sellable stock. A failure here blocks everything downstream and is visible physically (trucks waiting) long before any dashboard shows it. DUPLICATE_ACTIVE_GATEPASS is a legitimate floor - exclude it.

flow: Gatepass creation failing - goods stuck at the gate
what_breaks: Some gatepasses are failing to create
runbook: Usually one vendor or one carrier record. Check FETCH_CARRIER_ERROR in the same window.
notes: Carrier lookup failures surface separately as FETCH_CARRIER_ERROR - worth correlating rather than alerting on separately.

what_breaks: Gatepasses cannot be moved or cancelled, so they stay open. An open gatepass blocks the next one for the same warehouse+vendor+bill (DUPLICATE_ACTIVE_GATEPASS), which compounds into a gate blockage.
runbook: Check for gatepasses stuck open beyond a shift. Cancellation requires cancellationReason - a missing one is a 400, not an outage.
notes: Self-compounding: each unclosed gatepass blocks the next delivery from the same vendor, so the impact grows rather than staying flat.

what_breaks: Some gatepass status updates are failing
runbook: Check GATEPASS_DOCUMENT_UPLOAD_ERROR too - a failed invoice-document upload can block the status move.
notes: Max 10 invoice documents per gatepass; hitting that is a legitimate rejection.

flow: GRN cannot be started or resumed
what_breaks: Warehouse staff cannot begin or continue inwarding. Stock is physically on site but cannot be entered, so it never becomes sellable.
runbook: Check error_message for GRN_GATEPASS_NUMBER_REQUIRED or GRN_ALREADY_HAS_GATEPASS - both mean the gatepass step is wrong, so triage gatepass first.
notes: Triage upstream-first: a gatepass problem presents here as a GRN error. GRN_INVOICE_EXISTS_FOR_DIFFERENT_VENDOR_OR_WAREHOUSE and GRN_ALREADY_COMPLETED are legitimate rejections - exclude before thresholding.

flow: GRN cannot be started or resumed
what_breaks: Some GRNs are failing to start or resume
runbook: Draft-save failures are the quiet one - staff lose entered work and usually re-key it rather than report it.
notes: GRN_SAVE_DRAFT_ERROR is worth watching on its own: it loses operator work silently and generates no complaint, just slower inwarding.

flow: Bill creation failing - GRN cannot complete
what_breaks: The GRN cannot be closed into a bill, so the inward never finishes and the stock never reaches Zoho. Everything received in this window stays unsellable.
runbook: Check Zoho health first. If Zoho is fine, sample error_message - INVALID_GST_FOR_TAX_DERIVATION means a warehouse or vendor GSTIN is missing, which blocks tax derivation entirely.
notes: GST derivation failures are NOT separately visible: GRN_GST_DERIVATION_ERROR is declared in the enum but NEVER EMITTED, so a GST problem is indistinguishable from any other bill failure here. Worth emitting it - it is a distinct operational fix (add the GSTIN) from a Zoho outage.

flow: Bill creation failing - GRN cannot complete
what_breaks: Some bills are failing to create
runbook: Usually one vendor's tax setup or one batch failing PTR_CANNOT_BE_GTE_MRP.
notes: Data-quality rejections dominate this floor. Capture vendor + drugCode in triage.

what_breaks: The bill POST timed out AND the recovery search also failed. Zoho may hold a bill that we have nothing persisted for - the GRN is permanently wedged and the stock is in limbo between systems.
runbook: Search Zoho manually for the bill number + vendor. If it exists there, the local record must be reconciled by hand before the GRN can proceed. Do not simply retry - that risks a duplicate bill.
notes: Fires on a SINGLE occurrence deliberately. The code comment at zoho.service.ts:5973-5978 states the failure mode explicitly: failing here 'would orphan the bill on Zoho with nothing persisted locally and permanently wedge the GRN'. The adopt-existing path (CREATE_ZOHO_BILL_SKIPPED) is the healthy recovery; this code means even that failed.

what_breaks: Bill creation is timing out and being recovered by adoption
runbook: Recovery worked, so nothing is broken - but a rising rate means Zoho bill POSTs are getting slow enough to time out routinely.
notes: This is the SUCCESS path of the recovery, tracked as a leading indicator of Zoho latency rather than as a failure. If it climbs, expect grn-bill-wedged to start firing.

what_breaks: An unusual share of received stock is being blocked on expiry, PTR/MRP or MRP deviation. Almost always a vendor or purchase-order problem rather than a software one - but it stalls inwarding all the same.
runbook: Group by vendor. A single vendor dominating means a commercial conversation, not an engineering one. Expiry blocks require a Vendor Credit to return the stock.
notes: NOT an error signal - these are working-as-intended quality gates, which is why there is no critical row. Expiry rule blocks anything expiring within 1 month (Utils.isExpiryWithinBlockWindow). Route this to procurement, not to on-call.

what_breaks: GRNs are being started but not completed. Catches the silent case: staff can begin inwarding, hit a wall partway, and abandon - no error is raised and no alert above fires, but stock never becomes sellable.
runbook: Find GRNs created today with no matching completion. Check whether they are all at the same step - that identifies the wall.
notes: The inward equivalent of the invoice hang detector. A GRN spans a shift, so the window must be a day, not minutes - do NOT copy the short windows used elsewhere in these sheets. Note stock is NOT sellable at GRN_COMPLETED either: item_procurement.stock_in_warehouse is updated by a Zoho-pull cron, not synchronously by createBill (CLAUDE.md), so there is real lag between a completed GRN and sellable stock.

what_breaks: Fewer GRNs completing than usual for this day
runbook: Compare against the delivery schedule before treating as a fault - a light delivery day looks identical.
notes: Strong weekly seasonality tied to vendor delivery schedules. Baseline by day-of-week, not hour-of-day.

what_breaks: Stock is physically in the building but not being put away against a rack location. Pickers cannot find it, so it behaves as phantom stock: sellable on paper, missing on the shelf.
runbook: Check whether the racking task or the drug_warehouse_locations write failed. Stock racked without a location row is the worst case - it exists but no picker will be routed to it.
notes: Sits directly after GRN in the inward chain: gatepass -> GRN -> bill -> RACKING -> findable stock. A GRN can complete cleanly and stock still be unpickable if this fails. mdm.drug_warehouse_locations is the mapping (owned by pdp, endpoints in warehouse-operations).

what_breaks: Some racking tasks are failing to complete
runbook: Sample the taskId and tray. Repeats on one tray usually mean a scan/identifier problem, not code.
notes: Warehouse staff will re-try rather than report, so a low steady rate is invisible operationally. Watch the trend, not the spike.

flow: Rack location lookup failing - pickers blind
what_breaks: Rack location lookups are failing, so pick lists show no location. Pickers walk the floor searching, pick rate collapses and every order behind them misses its RFD.
runbook: Read path - check the last deploy first. Confirm mdm.drug_warehouse_locations is queryable; the idx_bill_items_drug_batch index dropped from that migration would also degrade this.
notes: Degrades throughput rather than stopping it outright, so it will not surface as an outage - it surfaces as 'picking is slow today'. Worth paging anyway because the cost compounds across every order in the shift.

flow: Rack location lookup failing - pickers blind
what_breaks: Rack location lookups failing intermittently
runbook: Check whether it is one warehouse - locations are per-warehouse.
notes: Per-warehouse mapping means one site can be blind while others are fine. Capture warehouseId.

what_breaks: A SKU has arrived with no rack location mapping, so it cannot be put away or picked until someone assigns it a home. Operational backlog rather than an outage.
runbook: Collect the drug codes and hand to the warehouse team to assign locations. Not an engineering fix unless the write itself is failing.
notes: No critical row: a missing mapping is a data-entry gap, and new SKUs legitimately arrive without one. Only alert if the volume suggests the auto-assign path itself broke. NOTE there is no RACKING_TASK_CREATED code, so a racking funnel (created vs completed) CANNOT be built today - RACKING_TASK_CREATE_ERROR and ADD_MISSING_RACK_LOCATION_ERROR are both declared-only and never emitted.

what_breaks: The 2-hourly job that moves RTO_INITIATED (107) to RTO_IN_TRANSIT (108) after 3 days has stopped. Returned parcels stall at the first rung, so nothing reaches the warehouse, no QC happens and no refund is triggered.
runbook: Check cron-job.org for POST /orders/updateRtoStatus (orders.controller.ts:2392). Scheduled every 2h per the cron inventory - so two consecutive misses is a real failure.
notes: This cron IS scheduled (unlike the transfer-order ones) - confirmed in the cron inventory as 'Update RTO InTransit Orders', every 2h. Set treatMissingData=breaching. GAP: the handler logs the REQUEST marker with no payload and returns {count} WITHOUT logging it, so there is no 'how many advanced' metric - add count to the log and this becomes a much better signal.

what_breaks: The RTO status cron is running but erroring
runbook: The whole sweep is inside one try/catch and rethrows, so ONE bad order aborts the entire run - the remaining orders are not advanced.
notes: Important shape difference from the transfer-order reconcile cron, which is per-item try/catch: here a single failure stops everything after it. That makes a single occurrence meaningful rather than routine.

flow: RTO refund not completing - customer out of pocket
what_breaks: Goods have come back but the refund has not. Orders sit at RTO_REFUND_INITIATED (160) without reaching RTO_REFUND_PROCESSED (161) - the customer has paid, returned the parcel, and has neither goods nor money.
signal: Orders at status 160 ageing beyond N hours
cloudwatch_filter_pattern: VERIFY: check whether UPDATE_ORDER_STATUS carries the status id in $.meta before using a metric filter; otherwise use a Metabase alert on marketplace.orders
runbook: Cross-check against the refund alerts in the main registry - an RTO refund failure is usually a gateway failure, not an RTO-specific one.
notes: Highest customer-anger case in the reverse chain and the reason RTO deserves its own rows at all. Signal needs confirming: status transitions may not carry the id in the log payload, in which case this is a Metabase/DB alert rather than CloudWatch.

flow: RTO refund not completing - customer out of pocket
what_breaks: RTO refunds are ageing
runbook: Check whether QC (125) completed for those orders - refund is gated on it.
notes: RTO refund is gated on RTO_QUALITY_CHECK_DONE (125), so a QC backlog presents here. Triage QC first.

what_breaks: An unusual number of returns are ending at RTO_LOST (117) or RTO_MISMATCH (120). Lost parcels are written-off stock and a refund liability; mismatches mean what came back is not what went out.
cloudwatch_filter_pattern: VERIFY as above - status id in log payload, else Metabase
runbook: Group by courier partner. A single carrier dominating LOST is a commercial conversation; spread across carriers suggests a warehouse receiving problem.
notes: Both statuses are money: LOST is written-off stock, MISMATCH is a dispute. Day-window because RTO transit takes days - do not use the short windows from the outward chain.

what_breaks: RTO losses or mismatches above normal
runbook: Route to the logistics team with the carrier breakdown rather than to on-call.
notes: Vendor-management signal more than an engineering one, same as the GRN quality gates.

what_breaks: Parcels marked RTO_DELIVERED (112) by the courier are not being received into the warehouse (113). Stock is at the door but never enters inventory, and the refund chain behind it never starts.
runbook: This is a warehouse-process gap more often than a software one - confirm with the site before raising a bug.
notes: The reverse-chain equivalent of the GRN funnel. Included as warning-only because the failure is usually operational; promote to critical if it proves to be a systems problem.
